title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 6-8). G is a reductive Q-group, presumably a candidate motivic or Mumford-Tate group. A 'rigidified G-subordination' on a complex analytic space S is a tensor functor V ↦ (Hodge structure on V_C × S). It is a real-analytic bigrading V_S^{p,q} with V_S^{q,p} equal to the conjugate of V_S^{p,q}, with weight given by the degree, Q(-1) of type (1,1), and fibrewise polarizable by a G-invariant form. Page 6 shows that, pointwise, such a datum is a homomorphism j(s): 𝕊 → G_R from the Deligne torus. Equivalently it is j'(s): U → G'_R with j'(-1) = η (a fixed central element) and the centralizer of j'(s) maximal compact. Page 6 also shows that j(s) depends real-analytically on s.

This page, step 1. Let D be the set of all admissible j (or j'). D carries a natural complex-analytic structure; implicitly it is an open subset of the compact dual flag variety G_C/P_j via j ↦ Hodge filtration. Holomorphy of the Hodge filtration of the family is then equivalent to holomorphy of the period map s ↦ j(s): S → D.

Step 2. Hence rigidified G-subordinations on S are exactly Mor_an(S, D). The functor S ↦ {rigidified G-subordinations on S} is representable by D: D is a fine moduli space for Hodge-theoretic G-structures with a trivialization of the underlying fibre functor.

Step 3. G(R) acts on D by analytic automorphisms, by conjugation. The orbits are open, I read the underlined word as 'ouvertes': homomorphisms from a torus are rigid. So each connected component of D is G(R)^0 / (H(R) ∩ G(R)^0), where H is the centralizer of some j: 𝕊 → G. Equivalently it is G'(R)^0 / (H'(R) ∩ G'(R)^0), with H' the centralizer of j': U → G'.

A crossed-out passage begins the arithmetic step. Take a faithful V and a lattice V_0 ⊂ V; then a G-subordination gives a Z-Hodge structure on V_0 × S; let Γ ⊂ G(Q) be the stabilizer of V_0. This aims at the quotient Γ\D. The next page carries the non-rigidified case through: monodromy α: π_1(S,s) → G(Q), plus a period map from the universal cover S~ → D.

What the page serves: a moduli description of families of Hodge structures with given 'motivic' group G, i.e. Mumford-Tate (Hodge) domains and their arithmetic quotients, in tannakian language. This is part of Grothendieck's 1965 programme around the motivic Galois group and the Hodge conjecture.
errors: Griffiths transversality is never imposed; only holomorphy of the filtration is. So D represents all holomorphic families of G-Hodge structures, not variations of Hodge structure in Griffiths' sense. Families coming from geometry land in the horizontal sub-bundle. Mor(S, D) and geometric VHS coincide only when the weight/type is Hermitian (Shimura) type, e.g. adjoint types among (-1,1), (0,0), (1,-1). This is not a logical error given his definition, but it is a significant gap for the intended application.

As machine-transcribed ('les orbites sont connexes'), the inference 'Donc les comp. connexes de D sont G(R)^0/…' does not follow. G(R)-orbits need not be connected, since G(R) is often disconnected. The needed (and true) statement is that the orbits are open, by rigidity of torus homomorphisms up to conjugacy. The underlined word in the image most likely reads 'ouvertes'.

The 'natural complex-analytic structure' on D is asserted without construction. Implicitly it comes from the open embedding of each G(R)-orbit in the flag variety G_C/P (Borel-type open orbit), which requires the polarizability/compactness condition. It is correct but unproven here.
Minor: the transcribed 'd: D → G' must be j: 𝕊 → G (the Deligne torus), consistent with page 6.

ideas.what: Space D of admissible Hodge cocharacters j: 𝕊 → G_R (or j': U → G'_R with j'(-1) = η central and maximal-compact centralizer), with a natural complex structure, as a period domain attached to a reductive group
ideas.modern_name: Mumford-Tate domain / G-period domain (homogeneous period domain G(R)/H(R)); the Shimura-datum conjugacy class X
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford (1966, Hodge groups of abelian varieties), Griffiths (period domains, 1968-70), Deligne (Travaux de Shimura 1971; Variétés de Shimura 1979), Green-Griffiths-Kerr (Mumford-Tate domains, 2012)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA. The tannakian Hodge viewpoint appears later in Saavedra Rivano (1972) and Deligne-Milne (1982).

ideas.what: Representability: rigidified tensor functors Rep(G) → {polarizable holomorphic families of Hodge structures on S} correspond bijectively to Mor_an(S, D); the period domain is a fine moduli space for framed G-Hodge families
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of period domains / framed variations of Hodge structure with G-structure (period map as a classifying map)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths (period map), Deligne; tannakian formulation in Milne's notes on Shimura varieties and in Klingler et al.
ideas.where_published: unsure; not in published Grothendieck texts to my knowledge

ideas.what: Conditions j'(-1) = η and Cent(j') maximal compact as the tannakian translation of polarizability
ideas.modern_name: Deligne's polarization criterion: Ad h(i) is a Cartan involution (axiom SV2-type condition)
ideas.where_published: Pages 5-6 of these same notes ('le th'); unpublished

ideas.what: Connected components of D are G(R)^0/(H(R) ∩ G(R)^0), with H the centralizer of a Hodge cocharacter (open orbits)
Crossed-out start: lattice V_0, arithmetic group Γ = Stab(V_0) ⊂ G(Q), leading (next page) to monodromy π_1 → G(Q) and the quotient Γ\D
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic quotients Γ\D (Mumford-Tate varieties, Shimura varieties); period map S → Γ\D

missed.claim: Priority/history. In 1965 Grothendieck had already formulated, in tannakian 'Rep(G) → Hodge structures' language, the period domain attached to a reductive group G (the Mumford-Tate domain). He gave Deligne-style polarization conditions on the cocharacter and stated its representability as a fine moduli space of rigidified families. This predates Mumford 1966, Griffiths 1968 and Deligne 1971, and these notes are not usually cited as a source for the group-theoretic (Shimura-datum-like) description.
missed.quote: Donc l'ens. des G-subordinations rigidifiées sur S s'identifie à l'ens. Mor(S, D) ... Donc pour S variable, on a un foncteur représentable par D.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents an early, independent Grothendieck source for the tannakian approach to Mumford-Tate domains and Shimura data. That approach is usually attributed to Deligne and Saavedra, and the page is relevant to histories of the motivic Galois group and of the Hodge-theoretic Shimura formalism.

missed.claim: The arithmetic step (lattice V_0, Γ ⊂ G(Q), quotient Γ\D as a moduli space of non-rigidified G-families) is begun and crossed out. Without Griffiths transversality, Γ\D would classify all holomorphic G-families, not geometric VHS. The interplay between this 'full' moduli and the horizontal one is not addressed.
missed.quote: Soit Γ ⊂ G(Q) le stabilisateur de V_0 [barré]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Modest. The distinction between horizontal and non-horizontal Mumford-Tate domains (classical vs non-classical) is now studied (Green-Griffiths-Kerr; o-minimal period maps). The note shows Grothendieck's setup tacitly fits only the Hermitian/Shimura case.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is now standard (Mumford-Tate domains, Shimura-datum axioms, period maps). What is notable is the date and the tannakian framing: a representability statement for G-period domains in 1965, before Mumford, Griffiths' general theory and Deligne's axiomatization. That is a historically interesting unpublished detail, though not new mathematics today; transversality is also missing.
transcription_corrections: 'les orbites sont connexes' — the underlined word is more likely 'ouvertes' (orbits are open), which is what makes the following 'Donc les comp. connexes de D sont…' valid.
'(and autom. analytiques[?])' should read '(par automorphismes analytiques)'.
'centralisateur d'un d : D → G' should be 'd'un j : 𝕊 → G' (Deligne torus), consistent with page 6.
'G-subordinations [-dans-] S' — the crossed-out word is replaced by 'sur S', and 'rigidifiées' is inserted above.
Opening sentence: 'la condition d'holomorphie de la filtration' (not 'fibration'), matching page 6.
In the boxed crossed-out passage, 'Soit ... V une G-subordination fidèle' is likely 'Soit V une G-représentation fidèle'; 'pas nécessairement isog' is likely '(pas mod isog)'.
